items.title:
New EIP!

Variable-Size Blobs

🔗 https://t.co/sZxQk9R81H

Highlights:
- Blobs b
items.summary:
New EIP!

Variable-Size Blobs

🔗 https://t.co/sZxQk9R81H

Highlights:
- Blobs become variable-sized codewords from 2,048 to 1,048,576 bytes (power-of-two, divisible by 128), keeping 128 columns but changing cell size accordingly (16 to 8,192 bytes).
- Commitments are length-bound: instead of committing only to a Merkle root, the commitment includes (root, blob_byte_length); signatures, challenge derivation, and versioned hashes must bind both so the same root can’t be reinterpreted under another size.
- Transactions are restricted to exactly one blob commitment (or zero for no-blob frame tx), replacing EIP-8479’s multi-blob-per-tx model; BLOBHASH returns only index 0 (others are zero).
- Validation and networking/consensus checks become size-aware: clients must reject invalid lengths early; cells returned over the network and included in sidecars must exactly match blob_byte_length/128, and verifiers use commitment.blob_merkle_root for root comparisons.
- Fees and limits are proposed but not finalized: a new per-blob ‘blob_gas’ equals nominal data bytes (byte_length/2) plus a fixed 4,064-byte Merkle internal-node allowance; schedule conversion and many activation details (fee transition, reserve-price interaction, EL/CL limits, profile negotiation, new guest program/keying) are explicitly unresolved and must be decided before activation.

ELI5:
Today blobs are “one fixed box size,” so if you only have a little data you still pay for a whole big box or wait to fill it. This proposal lets blobs come in different box sizes (from 2 KB up to 1 MB) while keeping the same internal 128-slice layout. To stop confusion or cheating, every blob’s commitment includes both its Merkle root and its byte length, and fees/accounting are updated to charge based on how much data is actually inside.

items.title: Configurable Accounts is the endgame design for crypto wallets at the protocol l
items.summary:
Configurable Accounts is the endgame design for crypto wallets at the protocol layer. 

Beyond the other good stuff i have talked about such as future proofing against cryptography attacks and scaling assets via multisigs, it enable a long envisioned pattern with @_jxom and @awkweb - guest checkout.

If you think about it - crypto onboarding sucks for two reasons, and we have solved both of them:
- logging in with a secure credential
- onramping with KYC

We solved the onramp with MACH- a select # of MPP services can enjoy embedded headless kycless onramping. LMK if you wanna try it.

For logging in, configurable accounts allow us to onboard a user w/ a browser held private key generated like a burner wallet. But at the end of the flow, you may add the passkey / google or whatever else as a signer and revoke the private key. 

Good UX sometimes doesn’t require removing friction, it means moving the friction AFTER the user is bought in, so they have an incentive to do the step.

These are some of the wonders you can achieve when you can co-design a protocol not just for performance and security but also for the wallet experience.

items.title:
On fighting propaganda, ACD, and what makes Ethereum special..

I’ve seen some p
items.summary:
On fighting propaganda, ACD, and what makes Ethereum special..

I’ve seen some people refer to ACD as some sort of institution that just picks what’s good for Ethereum on its own. 

While ACD has a lot it can do better, it’s important to know it’s more of a consortium than a centralized cabal. It literally stands for “ALL CORE DEVS” and represents multiple individual contributors and teams !! 

Like, YOU can join ACD. In fact, if it were some gatekept thing, 100% of its current members wouldn’t be there. Many members joined after The Merge, which inspired brilliant technical minds to come to Ethereum to help it fulfill its mission (and maybe something as ambitious as the Merge..*ahem ahem* PQAI can do the same). 

Now having said all that, there is a difference between a process that is hard to participate in because the work requires a certain level of technical fluency, and a process that is difficult to participate in because it’s gatekept. 

ACD doesn’t represent an institutional opinion because it mainly represents rough consensus amongst core devs. 
Also, even if EVERYONE on ACD agrees on something, Client Teams still need to implement it, and Node Operators still need to adopt it. It’s not like things just happen because ACD says so either. 

They literally fight all the time, in public, and you can see it all on an open call every week via Forkcast (https://t.co/Xj1GCkt5qX), thanks to @wolovim ! You’re welcome to fight with ACD too, but please don’t, there’s too much for them to do right now, so you’ll most likely end up fighting with me, and no one wants that. 

What makes Ethereum special is that its disagreements all happen in public, and its uncertainties and shortcomings are exposed to the whole world as they occur in real time. This sometimes makes Ethereum look more dysfunctional than projects whose disagreements all happen behind closed doors. 

Do I think some doors can be more open, or at least have a mailbox next to them? Sure. Do I think we have closed doors? No, but perhaps the stairs to get there should be easier. There must ALWAYS be more room for inquiry, but it’s quite remarkable that we have a 300B dollar decentralized network that lets any random internet critic become someone who may actively shape its development. 

No company or movement in this space has such open, decentralized development, and we should seek to protect this property as much as we seek to improve it

- FOCIL headliner status under review; decision deferred to next call (two weeks)

items.title: Ethereum core development is a big decentralised ship, which means it’s hard to
items.summary:
Ethereum core development is a big decentralised ship, which means it’s hard to change its course, somewhat by design, but also just due to its sheer size.

We can make the numbers and the talent we have work for us instead of against us, by being clear with the outcomes we want, precise in our strategy, and urgent in our execution.

This exercise makes me hopeful we both ship incredible things (brand new user-friendly account features, a new consensus model that unlocks so much more, leanVM as workhorse for aggregating everything and making the protocol’s data smol) and ride with style the tidal waves of improving AI capabilities.

If we play our cards right, we’ll come out the other side soon enough, looking at features such as faster slots and FOCIL, thinking they’re a piece of cake and natural to add on top of our hardened, pq-scaled protocol.

items.summary: When Binance’s hot wallets were drained on 29 October, the stablecoin issuers reacted fast: Tether froze the attackers’ main wallet 37 minutes after the stolen USDT arrived there, and Circle froze the USDC three minutes later ( Elliptic ). It was still a race. Several hundred million dollars of stablecoins had been swapped, sold or pledged as collateral before a freeze reached them. A freeze by address stops only what is still at that address , and ERC-20 gives an issuer nothing else: a balance

현재 이더리움의 글램스테르담 업그레이드가 지연된 이유 중 하나는 전체 스마트 컨트랙트의 최대 0.017%가 영향을 받을 수 있기 때문임.

이더
items.summary:
현재 이더리움의 글램스테르담 업그레이드가 지연된 이유 중 하나는 전체 스마트 컨트랙트의 최대 0.017%가 영향을 받을 수 있기 때문임.

이더리움이 이렇게 소수의 피해 가능성까지 고려한다는 것은 분명 이더리움만의 강점이라고 생각함.

하지만 모든 의견을 듣는 것과 모든 의견을 수용하는 것은 다름.

소수의 피해를 최소화하기 위한 노력은 필요하지만, 그것이 이더리움 전체의 발전을 저해한다면 어느 시점에서는 결단을 내려야 한다고 봄.

특히 이번 변경은 장기적인 이더리움의 확장을 위해 결국 거쳐야 하는 과정이기도 함.

Ethlabs 역시 충분한 검토 끝에 추가적인 수정이나 지연보다 기존 설계대로 업그레이드를 진행하는 것이 낫다는 입장을 밝혔음.

저 역시 이에 동의.

이더리움이 지향하는 가치와 철학은 존중하지만, 이해관계가 충돌하는 상황에서는 무엇을 우선할 것인지에 대한 기준이 명확해야 한다고 생각함.

이더리움과 ETH의 장기적인 가치를 높이는 방향이라면 이제는 과감하게 추진할 필요도 있다고 봄.

items.title: In October, an audit found that gas repricings in Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterda
items.summary:
In October, an audit found that gas repricings in Ethereum’s upcoming Glamsterdam hardfork break assumptions some deployed contracts rely on. As a result, the hardfork rollout was paused. Since then, Ethlabs has helped with the impact analysis and the exploration of paths forward. This has led us to conclude that the best way forward is to go ahead with Glamsterdam as is.

This is a difficult trade-off, and the problems found are serious and valid. Much of the disruption comes from repricing state creation, which is a necessary step on Ethereum’s path to 1000x scaling. The only option to avoid this would be to remove the relevant EIP outright, but this would give up Glamsterdam’s roughly 3x higher gas limit, and only postpone the problem to a later hardfork. A secondary source of the disruption is the new state gas reservoir. Here changes to the EIP could address some of the concerns, but only for a subset of affected projects and at the cost of further months of delay. On net, in our assessment, neither of these options pass the cost-benefit test.

There are important lessons from Glamsterdam on how to improve future hard forks. We need to flag disruptive changes early and bring app developers in, scope impact analysis more carefully for sensitive EIPs, establish a shared understanding of which invariants app developers can rely on, and provide new primitives where there are gaps today.

You can read our full writeup here: https://t.co/G0NMm3L7eE

items.summary:
어제 비트마인 주가가 11불까지 내려가면서
신저가를 찍고 원성이 자자해서 그런지 

톰리와 비트마인 공식 계정이 답변을 해줬네요.

1. 자사주 매입에 대해서 비마 계정은 면밀히 주시중.
2. 톰리는 보유 현금을 인용하여 Ammo(탄약)이라 남김.

뭐 제 생각에는 일단 하락장이 조금 길어지고 있기 때문에 돈을 아끼는 게 맞음.

1년 운영비가 그래도 1~2억달러 정도 되는 회사이고, 남은 현금이 3.8억이기 때문에 자사주 매입을 원없이 하기에는 살짝 모자른 수치임.

현금을 다 쓰고 나면 지금은 mNav가 박살났으니 ATM발행도 쉽지 않고, 우선주 발행을 해야되는데, 지금같이 고금리 상황에서는 불리하게 조달해야할 확률이 높기 때문에...
(지금이야 우선주 금액이 별로 크지 않은 것도 있어서, BMNP의 가격만 보고 그 금리에 조달할 거라고 생각하면 안 될듯)

나도 1~2주 전만 해도 왜 자사주 매입 안 하냐고 찡찡 거렸지만, 냉정하게 하락장이 얼마나 빨리 끝날지 예상 안 되는 상황에서는 아끼면서 최대한 신중하게 판단하는 게 맞지 않나 싶음. 톰 리도 그 말하는 거고.

결과적으로 자사주 매입하기에는 더 좋은 조건이 계속 나오고 있기도 하고 ㅇㅇ.
(뭐 주가 방어를 안 한다는 이미지만 제거하고 싶은 거 같음)

솔직히 매주 8-K 공시내고, 공식계정으로 대답도 해주는 거면 회사중에서 소통 ㅈㄴ 잘 되는거임.

암튼 비트마인이랑 톰리도 자사주 매입이랑 남은 현금 사이에서 최적의 판단을 내리기 위해 노력하고 있다.너무 걱정하지 말자.

items.title:
New post on Eth Research!

Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach

By:
-
items.summary:
New post on Eth Research!

Optimal Dynamic Fees for L2s: A Vault Approach

By:
- ulrych8
- Ulysse Pavloff
- @linoscope

🔗 https://t.co/mdbXrtKBL3

Highlights:
- Because breaking even only stops further losses, an L2 must use feedback from the vault balance (not just current L1 costs) to restore the vault to its target after shocks.
- Fee-setting can be framed as a control problem with vault dynamics V_{t+1}=V_t+F_tΛ−C_t, and two competing metrics: vault tracking error (ISE) versus fee-change volatility (QV).
- If you explicitly penalize fee changes, the optimal (LQR) fee rule includes “memory” of the previous fee: F_t=πF_{t-1}+(1−π)F*+k·ε_t; if instead you penalize deviation from break-even, a simple proportional rule F_t=F*+k_p·ε_t is optimal.
- The single parameter π controls the trade-off: higher π means smoother fees but slower vault recovery; lower π means faster correction but larger fee jumps. Recovery speed can be calibrated (e.g., deficit half-life ≈ 2/(1−π) intervals).
- In historical ETH-price replays, Arbitrum’s deployed-style rule appears competitive near its chosen aggressiveness; proportional control can yield smaller worst-case shortfalls at similar fee movement, and when fee caps bind during extreme cost spikes, reserve size matters more than the specific rule.

ELI5:
An L2 collects fees from users to pay Ethereum (L1) for posting data. It keeps the difference in a “vault.” If L1 costs suddenly jump, the vault can drop below where it should be. Even if the L2 later charges the perfect “break-even” fee, the vault stays low forever unless fees temporarily adjust to refill it. The article explains how to design a fee rule that uses feedback from the vault balance, balancing two goals: keep the vault near its target and avoid making fees jump around too much.

items.title:
New post on Eth Research!

FOCIL and Ethereum's PQ transition

By:
- jihoonsong
items.summary:
New post on Eth Research!

FOCIL and Ethereum's PQ transition

By:
- jihoonsong

🔗 https://t.co/HvEXKhv2Ow

Highlights:
- IL (Inclusion List) committee selection stays simple: under PQ Gasper it can remain “first 16 members of beacon committees,” while PQ Decoupled Consensus may choose alternatives like drawing from an Available Chain committee.
- Even before a full PQ transition, ILs can carry PQ transactions using large hash-based signatures (e.g., leanSPHINCS), because each IL has an 8 KiB transaction-bytes limit and can include at least one large-signature transaction without changing the IL building mechanism.
- If signature/proof aggregation is used, ILs may include recursive STARK proofs (e.g., from periodic mempool aggregation) to compress dependency/signature verification; this can speed up IL construction by reusing existing proofs, but needs benchmarking and careful engineering.
- Bandwidth, not mechanism correctness, is the main concern: ILs with BLS or leanXMSS appear manageable within realistic propagation windows, but ILs carrying large recursive proofs are likely too heavy unless mitigations (1-slot delayed enforcement or smaller IL committee size) are adopted.
- During payload building/processing, the EL can verify either raw signatures (no aggregation) or one recursive proof per IL (with aggregation); verification is likely parallelizable and not a bottleneck, while enforcement in PQ Gasper can still rely on fork choice reorgs, and enforcement ideas for PQ Decoupled Consensus are still being explored.

ELI5:
Ethereum wants to switch to “quantum-proof” signatures, but those signatures can be much bigger and harder to send around quickly. FOCIL is a feature that helps guarantee transactions get included by having special lists of transactions (inclusion lists) shared each slot. This article explains that FOCIL can mostly keep working during the quantum-proof upgrade, but Ethereum must watch bandwidth and timing so those lists and their proofs can still travel across the network in time.

items.title: Post Quantum Transaction Signatures #19 (2026-11-25)
items.summary:
Post Quantum Transaction Signature (PQTS) Breakout #19

parameter and aggregation strategy:
- Kev's proposed 3-stage approach: benchmark raw signatures first (no aggregation), then block-builder aggregation, then mempool aggregation
- Safe Transaction Service signature limit is <5 KB; current sphincs.art default params yield ~8 KB signatures (up from ~4 KB); Nico: at least 15% fewer verification hashes (30–40% with other parameter trades) without changing lifetime
- lightclient: aggregation unlikely in Hegota; EL blocks in the 2–4 MB range are manageable without it, helped by networking improvements such as not re-propagating signatures already in the mempool
- lightclient: users must migrate only once; shipping two SPHINCS variants would be a failure (Iván agreed in chat; Justin Florentine was open to two if aggregation proves incompatible)
- Kev: the group still lacks a process for choosing the mainnet parameter set (sig size, wallet/MPC needs, aggregation speed); the next devnet doesn't need to wait on it
- Toni: gas prices every byte, so bigger signatures cap throughput (fewer txs per block) rather than worst-case block size
- Pruning disputed: Matteo called the 4 KB option's tree pruning risky and privacy-losing; Nico said hardware wallet makers strongly prefer pruning as the simplest option

devnet and spec path:
- Agreed: target bogota-devnet-3 (not Daisugi) with leanSPHINCS and either PROOF frame or sig list — no aggregation
- PROOF frame vs. sig list still undecided; EL teams need to resolve it before the bogota-devnet-3 spec is finalized

organizational:
- Core discussion moved to Discord (pq-el, pq-networking, pq-cl, pq-general channels); Telegram channel to be closed
- EthPandaOps (Philip) migrated Daisugi testnet to larger infrastructure; Project 11 and Nethermind assisted
- Nico: deadline is end of January and December holidays reduce capacity; warns against keeping a parameter set the group learns nothing from

액션 아이템:
- Restart Daisugi with the latest Nethermind branch (sphincs.art default parameters) to start benchmarking; Antonio later said Daisugi isn't needed once bogota-devnet-3 carries the PQ changes
- Share alternative SPHINCS parameter sets (more permutation/aggregation-friendly, no experimental optimizations) for comparison
- Resolve PROOF frame vs. sig list to unblock the bogota-devnet-3 spec; discuss in pq-el Discord

items.title: FOCIL Breakout #47 (2026-11-24)
items.summary:
FOCIL Breakout #47 - November 24, 2026

pq focil overview:
- PQ FOCIL has two distinct problems: (1) PQ transactions in ILs, (2) ILs signed with PQ signatures — these are separable
- PQ signatures are 5–7 KB; worst case only 1 PQ tx per IL, but 16 ILs per slot = 16 PQ txs per block — deemed acceptable for early adoption
- Including STARK proofs in ILs (~300 KB each) requires major networking redesign; not feasible until after EIP-8288 + PQCL aggregation land
- Switching IL signatures from BLS to XMSS adds 2.4 KB per IL; attack surface is low (attacker can only cancel FOCIL for one slot), so not urgent

pq focil design parameters:
- IL committee size and propagation window are tunable knobs; reducing committee weakens censorship resistance but may be necessary for bandwidth
- Proposal: use n+1 slot inclusion (12-second extra propagation window) to reduce peak bandwidth for STARK-proof ILs; trades off some CR
- IL equivocation evidence gossip (propagating only IL headers) could save ~308×2 KB, but adds protocol complexity; not needed before STARK-proof ILs

eip 8288 and pqcl timelines:
- EIP-8288 being split into 3 sub-EIPs: (1) leanSPHINCS sigs — possibly H-star; (2) mempool recursive aggregation (leanVM) — not before I-star, ~mid-2028; (3) leanPCS proofs — I-star at best, more likely J-star
- pq-devnet-0 running PQ Gasper now; networking expected to be the bottleneck — real numbers still needed
- PQ Gasper vs. PQDC undecided; PQDC spec does not exist yet; if PQ Gasper still questionable in ~2 months (Jan), consider switching to PQDC
- Mehdi: PQ Gasper not looking great after 3 PQ sessions + devnet-0; PQDC preferred but more expensive; PQ Gasper reserved for catastrophic scenario

focil dfi discussion:
- Proposal to DFI FOCIL from Hegota and go all-in on PQ Consensus being discussed; soft consensus expected at ACDC Thursday (Nov 26); final decision targeted Dec 10
- Justin: given FOCIL's maturity and uncertainty around PQCL schedule, dropping FOCIL from Hegota unlikely to speed up PQ Consensus delivery

organizational:
- Next FOCIL breakout penciled in for Dec 8 (two weeks), before the Dec 10 ACDC decision call; holiday pause possible after that

액션 아이템:
- Separate PQ Gasper work into transferable vs. non-transferable components ahead of potential pivot to PQDC
- Review Jihoon's PQ FOCIL article and soispoke's Eth Magicians post ahead of ACDC Nov 26

PQ-CL Breakout #4 - November 24, 2026

testing progress:
- pq-devnet-0 stalled: clients generating XMSS keys at different times; some waited until last slot, requiring up to 2h for key gen under 12s constraint
- 55-slot reorg caused by late attestations; Geth rejected reorgs >32 slots; max reorg depth flag set to unlimited, chain slowly recovering
- Prysm and Grandine flagged as blockers; Ethlambda had no key-gen issues (cached quickly); Lighthouse pre-generated 256 epochs in advance

leanvm updates:
- LeanVM 0.17 released: FFI (not sidecar), 15% faster recursion, single binary with runtime CPU dispatch (AVX2/AVX512/GFNI), breaking change requiring coordinated update
- Trade-off available: 7.5% faster proving at cost of 15% larger proof size (~200–300 KB today); consensus not to optimize STARK until setup is finalized

staking contract:
- Staking contract moved to sys-asm repo (PR open); XMSS verifier is Solidity/EVM bytecode (using the Keccak opcode) in a separate contract, called via static call
- Concern raised: validators reusing BLS mnemonic for PQ keys could be problematic if mnemonic is later destroyed; ERC should allow independent mnemonic

erc key derivation:
- ERC PR open (ethereum/ERCs#2214): specifies derivation from mnemonic → seed → XMSS and VRF keys; ERC-2335 (JSON keystore) counterpart not started yet

aggregator role:
- Proposal to define a separate aggregator role (opt-in, balance-weighted selection) discussed; Potuz: adds enough complexity to warrant moving to PQ-DC instead
- Decision: defer aggregator role; avoid adding it to first PQ fork if possible; revisit when quick slots or faster finality are needed

networking:
- Kamil: Lighthouse branch implements fast-proof broadcast (Merkle-root signed chunks); simulations show 1.7 duplicate messages vs ~7 with gossipsub at 4K peers/32K validators
- Csaba: Prysm (Go) seacast implementation targeting end-of-day/tomorrow; compatible with Silver (vlad) implementation; single-client Kurtosis testing recommended before multi-client devnet
- Need for a shared P2P spec (message signing, chunking details) flagged; Kamil and Csaba to align on wire protocol before cross-client testing

p2p timing measurements:
- Mark: initial devnet-0 timing data showed attestations arriving up to 9s; Lighthouse fixes (correct CPU target, per-attestation sending) resolved the worst of it; committee proving starts at 4.5s, within 6s window
- Proposer/aggregator prover contention identified: if proposing slot S+2 and aggregating S+1, tasks compete for prover; Potuz: just drop the aggregate in that case

organizational:
- pq-devnet-1 notes page published; next devnet will NOT include fork transition or system contract testing — focus remains on timing/aggregation
- Call cadence reduced: tomorrow's call canceled; keeping Friday call; plan to reduce to 1–2 per week going forward

액션 아이템:
- All CL teams: fix XMSS key pre-generation/caching and add key-gen-rate logging so pq-devnet-0 can recover
- Review the key-derivation ERC (ethereum/ERCs PR 2214; mnemonic → XMSS/VRF derivation) for cryptographic correctness, including mnemonic-reuse safety

eip8288 forward compatibility:
- EIP-8288 (signature and proof aggregation): frames must be forward-compatible; primary change is removing the signature list in favor of a PROOF frame mode
- Goal: users should not need to change wallets again when aggregation (EIP-8288) ships; forward-compat design is the priority over incremental devnet updates

pq signatures and sphincs:
- PQ sigs without aggregation: even several hundred PQ sigs/block is only a few MB; aggregation is for efficiency, not security — don't block shipping

items.title: Post Quantum Transaction Signatures #17 (2026-10-28)
items.summary:
Post Quantum Transaction Signature (PQTS) Breakout #17 - October 28, 2026

testnet update:
- Testnet v03 launched on Daisugi (with Nethermind): single tx with STARK proof of 20 SPHINCS signatures under EIP-8288
- Post-DevCon testnet planned with EthPandaOps spam tooling for better benchmarks

sphincs parameter proposals:
- sphincs.art tool presented: explores SPHINCS parameter trade-offs (lifetime, shape, hash, FTS type) for Lean SPHINCS
- Default lifetime on sphincs.art is 2^30 (~1B signatures); reducing to 2^24 cuts size but raises key-rotation frequency
- Pruning improves keygen speed but leaks privacy after ~75 signatures; partial fix requires semi-trusted state, yields ~2,000 private sigs on Ledger
- Forest-of-WOTS FTS (Jonas Nick's sig.golf submission, Blockstream) gives >30% signing speedup but is novel, less MPC-friendly, and needs standard-model security proof
- Project 11 proposes two parameter sets: both use WOTS/WOTS+C, CAIC hash, lifetime 2^24; optimized for hardware wallets and MPC (SPHINCS G variant)

lifetime and key rotation debate:
- Bitcoin SPHINCS (Shrinks) currently at 2^40; Mikhail Kridinov open to lower values; Justin Drake advocates cross-chain alignment
- Circle hot wallets sign 30K–70K tx/day (~2^16–2^17); at 2^24 lifetime that is ~1.5 years before rotation
- Nico: surveyed 5 major exchanges — all said key rotation is trivially automatable; anything above 2^22–2^23 is sufficient
- Justin Drake argues for higher lifetime (2^30): easier UX communication, alignment with Bitcoin/Zcash, and room to reduce later
- Chat note: Bitcoin 2^40 accounts for off-chain protocols (e.g., high-volume Lightning nodes), not just on-chain use

mpc and hardware wallet constraints:
- WOTS forest is structurally worse for MPC (nearly 100% secret hashes vs ~50% for FORS); not just a compute-power problem
- Project 11: going from 2^24 to 2^32 is a make-or-break difference at the MPC layer, and rules out fast SPHINCS-G signing on a Ledger Nano S
- Justin Drake: proof-of-grinding via SNARK (host offloads grinding to laptop, proves correctness) expected to improve ~10x in ~12 months

액션 아이템:
- Circle (Daniel) to report internally on key-rotation feasibility and return with findings next call
- Emile to add 2^24 lifetime toggle to sphincs.art so parameter sets can be compared directly

- Edge cases: Reth skips SNAP 1, will support SNAP 2 in Glamsterdam; Nimbus EL can sync but not serve snap data

decoupled consensus simulation:
- Sukun presented decoupled consensus simulations (Cambridge workshop): decouple LMD-GHOST head vote (Goldfish) from FFG finality vote (Simplex); targets 4x faster finality
- Simulation: 500 cloud Prysm-fork nodes, 64 subnets, 2,500 validators/subnet (~25% above mainnet); Scenario 1 (staggered FFG) works but home nodes hit ~40 Mbps peak vs 25 Mbps limit
- EIP-8334 (bundle attestations): batching 4 votes reduces 960 bytes → 552 bytes; with partial messages, home node bandwidth drops well below 25 Mbps limit and Goldfish votes are >20% faster at P99
- Scenario 3 (3 committees/subnet, fully decoupled finality): works but Goldfish propagation degrades to ~1.2s without topic prioritization; topic priority work (Csaba) could resolve this
- Open design question: staggered publishing (Scenario 1) vs. multiple committees per subnet (Scenario 3); need to define desired properties before choosing

informed diffusion zcast:
- Csaba introduced zcast: fast & lean broadcast protocol built on segmentation, erasure coding, controlled I-have/I-want, and sampling; targets payloads and sampled broadcast, drawing its sampling ideas from FullDAS
- Benchmark: gossipsub today is far from optimal; zcast achieves sub-700 ms payload propagation with <2x bandwidth overhead even with 50 Mbps home builder uplink
- zcast is not designed for attestation aggregation (many-to-one / in-network compute); that remains a separate protocol domain
- Implementation: Go on top of go-libp2p/GossipSub + Python executable spec + formal modelling and verification (in progress); runs on Shadow and native QUIC; post on ethresear.ch with full technique breakdown
- Byzantine resilience tested up to 50% withholders and active malicious nodes; formal verification work ongoing to close remaining gaps

- Raise snap ENR behavior with Geth team; gather consensus on whether to include snap key and how to value it
- Share decoupled consensus simulation slides publicly for broader review

- Three strategies under simulation: (1) all FFG votes at slot start, (2) staggered per-second publishing, (3) three committees across slot; goldfish vote latency improves significantly in strategies 2 and 3
- Key problem: no cross-topic stream prioritization between goldfish and FFG meshes; QUIC stream priorities only work per-connection
- Plan: integrate GossipSub IHAVE/IWANT tracer; also attempt to make X-ray work with Shadow simulations

P2P networking #8 - September 09, 2026

client updates:
- Prysm: partial columns PR for Gloas fully reviewed/tested, awaiting one upstream PR before merge to release branch
- Prysm: peer scoring overhaul dev-complete; tested on Hoodi for one week, no regressions; adds per-agent observability and pruning metrics
- Lighthouse: fixing incorrectly ordered fields in partial messages; Gloas column gossip limit replacing static 8MB cap with dynamic limit based on blob schedule max
- Nethermind: sparse blob pool in master; working on IPv6 support, near completion

rowdas proposal:
- RowDAS adds row-based reconstruction duties to PeerDAS: vertical (distributed CPU across supernodes) and horizontal (supernodeless fallback) reconstruction
- Each supernode assigned a row duty (no custody requirement); duty-sharded variant skips row topics entirely, using only column topics — simpler first-stage option
- KZG reconstruction per blob ~162ms single-core; RowDAS reduces per-node CPU ~2 orders of magnitude; degrades to PeerDAS levels under adversarial conditions
- Implemented on Csaba's Prysm branch (on top of partial messages); row-based reconstruction without supernodes confirmed working at 65+ nodes

fast payload broadcast:
- 1MB payload over 50 Mbit uplink nodes (min-spec): current gossip-sub delivers last node in ~5s; all segmentation variants (A/B/C) converge near ~1s
- Variant A (normal gossip-sub + 32KB segments): 1.7s → 1.0s with batch publishing → further gains with phase-aware forwarding and disciplined pull (one requester per segment)
- Merkle commitment in the bid required to authenticate segments without full block; enables immediate per-segment forwarding upon receipt of signed beacon block
- ethp2p broadcast already implements chunking, push→pull phase transition, and pluggable nil encoder; Raúl offers to onboard collaborators and align with Csaba's work

eip proposals hegota:
- EIP-8411 (fast payload broadcast): replaces execution-payload topic with execution-payload-chunks; 64 segments, Merkle inclusion proof per chunk, payload-chunks-root added to bid; no erasure coding in v1 for simplicity
- EIP-8411 requires consensus change (bid field extension); without it, mixed-mode operation is possible but increases attack surface and buffering burden

ethp2p progress:
- Raúl implementing shared QUIC transport for Prysm: single endpoint serves both libp2p and ethp2p streams; stream routing via ALPN negotiation + first-byte slash detection; backwards-compatible with libp2p-only peers
- ethp2p payload broadcast branch hooked into Glamsterdam in Prysm; ready for DevNet testing
- Raúl previewed unified Ethereum networking specs site aggregating consensus-specs, EIPs, and ethp2p/Waggle specs in one taxonomy; unreleased, targeting this week
- ethp2p advantages over libp2p: unidirectional streams, datagrams, zero-RTT, session resumption, per-chunk stream interruption, slot-scoped cache lifetimes; lambdaclass has WIP Rust implementation

- Csaba and Raúl to align benchmarks and share code between simulation frameworks (Plisma vs ethp2p)

items.title: Post Quantum Transaction Signatures #14 (2026-09-02)
items.summary:
Post Quantum Transaction Signature (PQTS) Breakout #14 - September 2, 2026

sphincs parameter overview:
- Lean SPHINCS chosen as PQ replacement for ECDSA; no cryptographic precompiles will be shipped; aligns with hash-based consensus/DA layer direction
- Moving away from Poseidon toward Blake/SHA via new 'Flock' system on Banner Fields; specific hash function TBD
- NIST April 2026 SPHINCS variant cuts signature from ~8KB to ~4KB but requires 1.45B hashes to sign — impractical for hardware wallets
- SPHINCS Minus C12 targets 2^14 signature budget (covers 99.99% of mainnet addresses); signing cost 37K hashes vs. 1.45B; still 47.5s on Ledger Nano S
- Riva Labs achieved 1.5s signing on Ledger Nano S Plus (2^24 budget) via offline precomputation of public values + grinding; paper forthcoming

pq1 hardware wallet demo:
- Freedom Factory PQ1 wallet: STM32U585 (Cortex-M33) + NXPSE050 secure element; XOR key split via TrustZone; SPHINCS Minus C10
- On-chip signing: ~1.1s; cold boot (with key derivation): ~3s; SHA-256 hardware accelerator on STM32 aids performance
- First EVT hardware received; all code open source (WIP); STM32U585 eval board ~$100 total to run today
- Targeting Q4 2026 consumer device availability; uses account abstraction (modified base smart account), not native ECDSA replacement
- Verification contract in Trail of Bits audit; exploring Lean/eCrypt formal verification via Rust-to-Lean toolchain

mldsa evm optimization:
- Fireblocks (Oren): MLDSA-44 EVM verification reduced from ~8M gas to 1.2M gas (6× improvement); FIPS-compliant, open source, research quality
- Key registration (one-time expanded key stored on-chain, ~20KB) costs ~4M gas; full cold verification ~9M gas unoptimized
- Main savings: eliminating quadratic memory expansion (~2M gas saved), 256-bit batched lane operations, Yul/assembly rewrites; ~10% further reduction possible
- At current gas prices, 1.2M gas verification costs ~$0.22; contract to be published same day or next
- Result supports community position against MLDSA precompile for Hegota; pure EVM sufficient at this gas cost

액션 아이템:
- Publish optimized MLDSA-44 EVM verification contract to announced repository
- Share Lean/eCrypt formal verification progress for SPHINCS firmware with community
